question.text: The SEBI (AIF) Regulations permit an AIF to be formed as any of the following EXCEPT:

answer.text: Trust under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882
Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 138 and 487-488, the permissible legal forms for an AIF are Trust, Company, LLP, and Body Corporate. Sole proprietorship is not on this list. Per page 131, an AIF must have a distinct legal identity separate from its sponsor/manager, which a sole proprietorship does not provide. The Trap: Options A, B, and C are all permitted forms. Option D is excluded because a sole proprietorship lacks a distinct legal identity from the individual proprietor. Note: The "Body Corporate" route widens the eligible forms beyond Trust/Company/LLP, but it still requires a distinct juridical entity established under an Act.
